To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the monomer-d dimer ratio of human cyatin C can be governed by single amino-acid substitution in the hinge-region loop L1.
the monomer-d dimer equilibrium of human cystatin can be governed by the single amino acid substitution of the hinge region.

1) the L1 loop of cystatin C is important for its dimerization and 2) the L1-loop dimerization of cystatin C can be controlled by a single amino acid substitution, i.e. the dimer fraction can be increased (by introduction of proline) or decreased (by introduction of asparagine or aspartate) compared to the wild-type protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the dimerization mechanism of human cystatin.
the study of the role of the loop 1 in the dimeserization of human cystatine C.
the mechanism of dimerization and the influence of single amino acid substitutions on the monomer-dimers equilibrium in the human cystatin C protein.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dimerization is governed by the loop L1, but that this process is also influenced by other structural features of the protein.
the loop L1 is not a structural element of the cystatin C dimer but it is rather a structural determinant of the monomeric cystatin C.
loop L1 is important in the monomer-dimers equilibrium of human cystatin, however the role of the loop is not limited to its ability to act as a flexible turn.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dimerization is governed by the monomer-dominant wild-type protein, and the dimerization can be controlled by the introduction of turn-favorable amino acids in the hinge loop L1.
the loop L1 is a flexible loop that can adopt two distinct conformations in the monomer and dimer states.
cystatin C dimerization can be controlled by single amino acid substitutions in the hinge region.
The main takeaway from our work is that
loop L1 of cystatin C is important for its dimerization and the monomer-dimere ratio of cystatin C can be controlled by single amino acid replacement in this loop.
the loop L1 may be a potential site for rational design of human cystatin mutants with altered dimerization properties.

the dimerization propensity of human cystatin can be controlled by single amino acid substitutions, thus providing a new tool for studying this process and for engineering cystatin C variants with different dimerization propensities.
